title: Preemptive fallback policy rewrite for small-tenant burst handling
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: A subset of small, high-churn tenants experienced repeated allocation failures during short burst windows. Symptoms included request queuing > SLO, silent eviction from warm slots, and inability to acquire burst tokens despite apparent headroom in the pool. This ticket tracks a policy-level rewrite of the fallback and eviction heuristics that govern reserved-pool burst assignment for low-cardinality tenants, plus the short-term mitigations, customer comms, and rollout plan.

Why this matters: multiple enterprise customers reported degraded throughput during peak events, triggering P0 escalations. Existing fallback routing preferred cold-start alternatives that create an allocation storm and inhibited fair rebalancing. We observed situations where the burst ledger and the lease-renewal window race led to transient starvation for small tenants that rely heavily on burst credits.

Goal: implement a deterministic prioritized fallback that: 1) prevents eviction of recently-warmed slots for active bursts, 2) staggers lease reclamation to avoid synchronized reclaims, and 3) introduces a short-lived local credit buffer for tenants below N concurrent slots to smooth microbursts. Deliverables: code change in autoscaler, unit+integration tests, dashboards/alert updates, staged rollout, post-deploy validation, and customer followups.
updates: 2026-02-18: On-call flagged increased 99th latency for dedicated pools in us-west-2. Initial triage found a cluster of customers with repeated allocation timeouts during 30-90s spike windows. Pager and Slack notif created.
2026-02-18: Reproduced locally with load-generator using bursty arrival pattern; observed eviction thrash when pool headroom oscillated and burst tokens were simultaneously consumed and reclaimed.

2026-02-19: Root cause hypothesis: lease-reclaim scheduler aligns with burst-credit rebalancer, causing synchronous token drains and immediate slot eviction for tenants under the warmup threshold. This exacerbates allocation latency for microbursts.

2026-02-20: Short-term mitigation deployed: increased per-tenant soft-hold window from 5s -> 15s and disabled aggressive preemptive eviction for tenants with <3 active slots. Reduced customer complaints by ~60% but did not fully eliminate the problem.

2026-02-21: Customer comms: Sent interim status update to affected customers (AcmeHealth, NimbusAI); included temporary mitigation and ETA for permanent fix. Doing proactive credits for impacted tenants per CS request.

2026-02-24: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Decided on three-pronged approach: 1) policy rewrite to add deterministic tenant priority levels for fallback routing, 2) introduce a tiny local burst buffer for small-tenants (configurable), 3) de-synchronize lease-reclaim timing with jitter and backoff.

2026-02-27: Implemented policy prototype and added end-to-end integration tests in autoscaler module. New tests simulate N=100 small tenants with microburst patterns and verify no tenant experiences >2x baseline allocation latency.
2026-03-01: Code PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14286 (autoscaler: computed-priority fallback + local-buffer). Added feature flag dedicated.fallback_v2.

2026-03-03: Load staging: rolled feature flag on for limited staging pool. Observed 45% reduction in eviction events and smoother tail-latency during synthetic spikes. Captured additional telemetry to refine backoff constants.

2026-03-05: Found edge-case where local-buffer could be starved if tenant had sustained high throughput immediately after burst; added token replenishment decay and per-tenant max-burst-window to prevent abuse.

2026-03-07: Security/infra review passed. Added instrumentation: metric reserved_pool.fallback_v2.evictions, reserved_pool.local_buffer_hits, reserved_pool.reclaim_jitter_seconds. Created dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/dedicated/overflow-fallback-v2.

2026-03-09: Canary rollout schedule approved by SRE. Plan: 2-hour canary in us-west-2 small pool, monitor eviction and latency for 60m baseline then 60m spike, then 24h observation. Escalation path defined if customer latency > SLO or error-rate increases >0.3%.

2026-03-10: Canary started at 03:00 UTC. Early signal: local_buffer_hits increased as expected; tail latency for affected tenants dropped by median 28% and p99 by 43%. No new regression signals in other metrics. Continuing canary and preparing gradual region rollouts.

Next steps: finish additional integration tests for heavy sustained loads, complete QA checklist, finalize rollout notes, and prepare post-deploy summary for customers and incident timeline for runbook inclusion.
